text:
ABSOLUTELY AVOID: A Disgusting, Unsafe, and Overpriced Disaster
This is not a functioning McDonald's; it is a public safety hazard and an absolute disgrace to the brand. The location at 7th Ave & Van Buren is, without hyperbole, one of the worst dining experiences I have ever endured. I would give it zero stars if possible.
Environment and Safety: Unacceptable
The setting is immediately hostile and uncomfortable. The exterior and the interior dining area are filthy. The seating area reeked of an unmistakable stench of homelessness and pervasive funk, making it impossible to sit down comfortably. Outside, the property is overrun by groups of drug addicts and junkies, creating a profoundly unsafe atmosphere. The automated "no loitering" message playing endlessly over the loudspeaker was a pathetic, ineffectual attempt at control that only highlighted the total lack of actual management.
Service and Food Quality: Failures on All Counts
The service was glacial, suggesting zero interest from the staff in serving customers. Several employees appeared to be impaired or completely disinterested. When the food finally arrived, it was cold—the fries were stale, and the burger felt like it had been sitting for an hour, not prepared fresh. For an establishment that continually raises its prices, serving cold, subpar food is an insult to the customer.
The Bottom Line
The price gouging, the cold food, the rude staff, and the utterly disgusting and unsafe environment make this location unconscionable. I strongly urge the franchisee and corporate management to address this immediate crisis of quality and safety.
Future Customers: Drive Past!
Do yourself a huge favor and drive the extra distance to the McDonald’s at 35th Ave & Van Buren or 7th St & Durango. Not only are those locations clean and offer better customer service, but their prices are often slightly cheaper. This 7th Ave location is actively driving customers away. AVOID.
author: Ashantis Payne

text: I called in to ask about my order as it's been wrong now the last 3 times. We are in a homeless shelter and unfortunately can't cook and there is no food except what you buy... I get the cheapest meal at McDonald's. I called in and a young man answered. It wasn't during peak hours because I know they are under staffed at that point. Anyway. When he was very rude, I asked his name.  He said his name was Sam, and he was the owner.  I said okay so, your name is Sam what, he said I'm the owner the district owner. Lol I said okay, well if you're the district manager, you have a card then, correct, and I've never heard of anyone of high up working the night shift, as in 12:24a. I said, sir, I'm just trying to ask that it's made correctly. He said "do yo thang, mama!" It's so hard to find anything cheap to eat, not to mention that it's not good for you, but then to be treated this way, was very disappointing and frustrating. I've been looking for a job for a while now, I have a degree and years of experience and I can't get one, but someone like this is paid to treat people this way. I really hope Sam Jones, the "district owner of this location" has a better night, because clearly he wasn't happy when i called.
